world.bio: Pediatric occupational therapist at a small clinic in Austin, working mostly with autistic kids aged 3 to 10. I keep a running list in my phone of ordinary experiences families tell me their kids have never managed: a haircut, a birthday party, a movie theatre, a live concert. Engaged, planning the wedding on a tight budget, fostering kittens for the shelter, and taking a pottery class on Thursdays.
skills_assets: MS in occupational therapy, licensed in Texas, SIPT-trained, six years of pediatric experience
Families' trust: a caseload of 28 kids and their parents
A small clinic sensory gym with swings, weighted blankets, noise-cancelling headphones for loan
Access to the clinic's community outreach budget: $2,000, to be used by spring 2027 on a community event
A notebook titled 'Never Yet', listing 63 experiences families say their kids have never had
Foster kittens, currently three, named after Pixar characters

projects.name: Sensory-friendly afternoon (spring 2027)
projects.text: Families keep telling me their kids have never been to a live concert. I want to organise a sensory-friendly afternoon next spring, with lower volume, dimmed lights, a quiet room, a visual schedule, and no pressure to sit still. My clinic gave me an outreach budget of $2,000. I don't know yet what the afternoon looks like: a small live music event, maybe with local musicians, in a space where families won't be judged. Still very early, so I haven't told the families.

projects.name: Wedding planning
projects.text: Wedding in May, forty guests, backyard at my fiance's parents' house in Round Rock. Budget is $11,000 total. We argue about the playlist.

projects.name: Pottery class
projects.text: Thursday evenings at a studio on East Cesar Chavez. Currently struggling with a bowl that keeps collapsing.

notes.text: Had a session with Eli today, 6 years old. He sat on the swing for forty-five minutes without a meltdown. His mum cried in the waiting room. I did not. I cried in the car afterwards, and ate a granola bar.
Foster kittens ate through two electrical cords this week. I'm going to be broke on cords. Named the third one Woody. He has no idea.

A mum told me her son, Marcus, 8, has never been to a live concert. 'We tried once, the sound was too much, we left after four minutes,' she said. I wrote it on the list. Number 41, I think. It's been bothering me all week.
Wedding budget meeting with Jake. We have $11k. Food truck is $3,200. Photographer is $2,500. We cut the photographer's second shooter. He seems fine, I'm not.

Thinking about the $2,000. Clinic director said it must be community-facing, documented, and spent before the end of the fiscal year in June 2027. I keep returning to the concert idea. What would it look like? A band at a park? A school gym? Hard to say.
Pottery: my bowl collapsed again. The teacher said 'you're rushing the pull.' Was that about the clay or about my life?
Dad called, asked if we have a date. I said May 22. He said 'good, I'll be there with my knee'. He had a knee replacement in July.
Session with Lila, she hates loud noises but loves the piano. Her mum said 'she's never been to a concert and she'd probably love one if it were quiet'. I wrote it down, underlined it.

messages.text: Jake: I think we should use my cousin's playlist. Me: Your cousin's playlist is mostly Creed. Jake: He's a DJ. Me: He's an accountant who DJs on weekends. Jake: Fine, we'll compromise.
Dr. Patel: Maya, the outreach budget is yours. Me: Thank you, I'm thinking about a sensory-friendly event. Dr. Patel: Make sure we have liability coverage. Me: Understood.

Mum: Hi Maya, he had a good week. Me: That's wonderful. Mum: I keep thinking about what you said, that there might be a concert he could handle. Me: I'm exploring it. Mum: Please tell me if it happens.
Coordinator: Can you take two more kittens? Me: I have three. Coordinator: One's got an eye infection. Me: ...Okay.

relations.about: Fiance, software engineer, easygoing, wants a smaller wedding than she does.
Clinic director, supportive, cautious about liability.
Single parent, a nurse, works nights, very protective.

constraints: $2,000 budget must be spent by June 2027 on a community-facing event
Event must meet liability and accessibility requirements
sensitive: Anxiety about being the one organiser; afraid of letting down families
Her mother passed away three years ago
Worried about balancing work and wedding
